references.text: Jesus emphasizes again that he does not act on his own authority but only does what the Father has shown him, and that he always does what is pleasing to the Father.
Jesus confirms that his teaching and message do not come from himself but from the Father who sent him, and that he speaks only what he has heard.
Jesus explains that the words he speaks and the works he does are not his own, but the Father who dwells in him is completing his works.
The image of the vine and the branches illustrates the principle that a branch cannot bear fruit by itself but must remain in the vine to be able to do anything.
Jesus testifies that he has finished the work the Father gave him to do, and that he has not acted on his own will.
The psalm being quoted shows the Messiah's willingness to do God's will, to come to do God's will, and to complete what is determined.
